text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Elevated 429s observed for tenant AcmeCorp (tenant_id=acme-47) on Dedicated Pool cp-47 in us-west-2. Spike started ~3m ago, affecting generation endpoints and streaming. Support ticket #INC-12345 created. @samantha (oncall) please ack and triage.
samantha (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Setting context: Dedicated pool, rate limit is per-tenant token bucket with contract override flag. First checks: 1) Are we hitting token bucket limit or upstream Nginx 429s? 2) Any recent deploys to cp-47?
eng-sre: Looking at metrics now. CPU/GPU utilization on cp-47 is normal. Error rate shows 429 count spike concentrated at /v1/generate for tenant acme-47. Redis per-tenant counters show burst > contract qps for last 5m.
michael (support): Customer POC (jen@acme) just DM'd support: "Our dashboard stopped getting responses, getting 429s, it's blocking their demo." They mention a sudden automated test run.
lina (CSE): I messaged the POC to tell them we're working it. They said they recently started a stress job from multiple CI agents. Could be a misconfigured load test.
samantha (oncall): Good. eng-sre - can you confirm whether contract override is enabled for Acme? If the contract allows emergency lifts, we may approve a temporary increase. Also check tenant isolation config (no cross-tenant bleed).
eng-sre: Contract override flag is currently false. Their committed capacity is 2k QPS aggregated; observed 8k QPS burst. No recent deploys (deploy-bot shows last deploy to runtime was 6h ago).
alex (ops): If we do an emergency lift we need SRE approval + audit log entry. Lifting will change rate_limit_override for tenant which can increase billing exposure. Suggest temporary 15m lift to 10k QPS while we contact Acme.
michael (support): Acme's contract: Tier Enterprise-Plus. There is an emergency clause for demo disruptions. We can authorize a temporary override if SRE ok. POC confirms they need immediate lift to finish demo.
samantha (oncall): SRE, please confirm risk. What's the mitigation plan if this causes capacity pressure for other tenants in cp-47?
eng-sre: Risk: cp-47 has headroom for now but other tenants could be impacted if burst persists. Mitigations: 1) apply tenant-specific override (no change to pool-level queueing) 2) adjust routing policy to divert some non-critical tenants to backup pool (if compatible) 3) if necessary, throttle background batch jobs for certain customers. Option 1 is fastest.
lina (CSE): Customer is ok with a short window. They asked for 30m.
samantha (oncall): Ok do a 20m emergency lift, monitor metrics, and plan rollback or extension if needed. Alex, can you make the change and post the command you ran? Include audit note.
alex (ops): Running admin API now. Command:```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/acme-47/override" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"rate_limit_override_qps":10000,"expires_in_minutes":20,"reason":"Emergency lift for Acme demo - support ticket INC-12345","approved_by":"samantha"}'
```
alex (ops): Response: 200 OK {"tenant_id":"acme-47","new_qps":10000,"expires_at":"2024-06-05T15:42:30Z"}. Audit entry created: audit_id=audit-7789.
eng-sre: Saw the change land. 429s dropping immediately from 18%->1.5% on /v1/generate for acme-47. Pool latency unchanged. Keeping close eye on queue depth.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation applied by alex (ops). Marker: mitigation_type=rate_limit_override, mitigation_id=mit-20240605-01.
michael (support): Updated ticket INC-12345: "Temporary QPS increase approved and applied. Please confirm your job is completed and we'll monitor for 20m."
lina (CSE): Customer POC: "Thanks, demo resumed! We're running now."
samantha (oncall): Monitoring metrics and top talkers. If we see cross-tenant impact, we'll revert and coordinate a different plan. Also creating onboarding task for customer to configure CI test-rate limiting on their side.
eng-sre: Noted a handful of background tenants showing minor increased latency but not errors. If this degrades, we have fallback policy to route low-priority traffic off cp-47.
alex (ops): I'll schedule a manual rollback at expires_at if no extension requested. If they need longer, we'll escalate for formal contract amendment and charge adjustments.
michael (support): Customer confirmed job finished. POC: "Looks good, all tests passed"
incident-bot: Scheduled reminder for rollback at 2024-06-05T15:42:30Z.
samantha (oncall): Preparing handoff: @eng-sre will own post-mortem and capacity follow-up. I'll put a note in on-call rotation that I handled the emergency lift. Action items: - eng-sre: root cause analysis (why CI burst exceeded expectations) - Lina (CSE)/Support: recommend customer rate-limit guards - Product: consider adding UI affordance for self-service emergency lifts for Enterprise contracts
eng-sre: Acknowledged. I'll collect traces, per-tenant request patterns, and Redis key TTLs. Planning postmortem doc and will include timeline + suggested config defaults.
alex (ops): Rollback executed at expires_at. Command logged: admin API revoke override -> 200 OK. Audit audit-7790.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident resolved. Final check: 429s for acme-47 baseline back to expected levels. Ticket INC-12345 will be closed after postmortem.
samantha (oncall): Closing thread and filing postmortem link in ticket once ready. Thanks everyone. :slightly_smiling_face:
